messages.subject: Re: weights matchit
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marta,
I don't know if it is possible to automatically  incorporate weights into any of the propensity score approaches.  (The topic of combining weights and propensity scores is generally somewhat underdeveloped).

But this paper of mine may be helpful:  http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23855598

And some quick notes:
- It is useful to think separately about the propensity score estimation and then use
- It is also important to think carefully about the estimand of interest (see the paper above)
- In the propensity score estimation procedure one option is to include the weight as a covariate, essentially using it as a variable to match on
- After the propensity scores are estimated and used it is usually fairly straightforward to incorporate survey weights in the final outcome analyses (again, see the paper linked above)

I hope this helps!

Liz

messages.subject: Problem with K2K in CEM
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I intend to use a matching procedure on a project where, because of the nature of my cases, weights of control units should be all kept at 1. Reading the manuals and articles I realized that the way to do it was using CEM and applying the function k2k.However, I couldn't get it to work as described. When I run the command matchit(x, ..., k2k=TRUE), it returns a matrix that, when extracted into a data-frame, still contains weights and a different number of treated and control units - even though no error messages are shown. This happens both to my data and when running the lalonde demo script. The result of the matching is exactly the same as that obtained when k2k=FALSE. I tried to go back to the "cem" package and run the demo script there on LL with k2k - using first the command cem(x,... k2k=TRUE) and also doing the matching first and applying k2k(cem.match,...) afterwards. In both cases there's the error message "In min(x, na.rm = TRUE) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf", and the resulting matrix is still exactly the same as that obtained without setting k2k to TRUE.
Thank you in advance for the help.
Best regards,
Bruno Castanho e Silva

> 1:1)  in match.data function on in other way?

> For example  subject 122 is matched with subject 150  so this two subject
> would have the same valu of matching variable

> That is, a variable (zzz)  where all the members of any given match have
> the same value of zzz, and zzz is unique for each set.

You can easily peruse each treated observation against the match that was
obtained for it. However, the theory is grounded on the idea that the
_distribution_ of the treated observations is as close as possible to the
_distribution_ of the controls. Whether one particular observation is much
like its control is just a curiosity.

--
